card.title: SNES Super Nintendo Entertainment System

claims.statement: SNES no power: check the adapter (9 V DC or AC; Super Famicom barrel is centre-ground/outer-positive, US/EU centre-positive), the floating fuse near the power jack, the 7805 output and the input choke; discharge the main cap before working inside.

Black screen with signal: check /RESET at CIC U8 pin 10 / PPU2 U3 pin 34 is high; /RESOUT0 (PPU2 pin 33) and /RESOUT1 (pin 28) low while /RESET high = replace PPU2; no RGB/CSYNC on PPU2 pins 95–97/100 = PPU2, else S-ENC U7.
Garbled sprites or burn-in test OAM / OBJ L OVER failures = replace PPU1; HV TIMER failure = replace CPU; no audio = PPU2 (per source).

Left audio dead is commonly leaking C59 eating the trace under the C59/C60 labels: bodge R70 to the C66 test point and replace C59 with 10 µF 50 V non-polarised (or omit it, losing only 12 V on the AV port).
S-ENC comes in Nintendo-branded and BA6592F variants that aren't drop-in interchangeable; banding with tinted colours means replace S-ENC.

procedure: Inspect for leaks and corrosion; discharge the main cap.
Check adapter, fuse, 7805 and choke for no-power.
Use a burn-in test cart to classify chip faults.
Follow reset/PPU/S-ENC signal checks for video faults.
Repair C59 trace for left-audio faults.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: The main filter cap stays charged; discharge it before working inside.
card.caveats: Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
